primary.outcome_definition: Primary Composite Endpoint of Doubling of Serum Creatinine (DoSC), End-stage Kidney Disease (ESKD), and Renal or Cardiovascular (CV) Death

outcome_definition_source.description_verbatim: Primary composite endpoint is the composite of DoSC, ESKD, and renal or CV death. DoSC: from baseline average determination (sustained and confirmed by repeat central laboratory measure after at least 30 days and preferably within 60 days). ESKD: as initiation of maintenance dialysis for at least 30 days, or renal transplantation, or an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) value of less than (<)15 milliliters per minute per 1.73 square meter (mL/min/1.73 m^2) (sustained and confirmed by repeat central laboratory measure after at least 30 days and preferably within 60 days). Renal death: death in participants who had reached ESKD, died without initiating renal replacement therapy, and no other cause of death was determined via adjudication. Adjudication of these events by Endpoint Adjudication Committee (EAC) was performed in blinded fashion. Event rate estimated based on time to first occurrence of primary composite endpoint are presented.

primary.poolable_reason: WITHHELD on two independent grounds, each established from a source and each sufficient on its own. (1) THE THREE TRIALS DO NOT SHARE ONE ENDPOINT DEFINITION. All three composites count kidney-function decline, but at three different thresholds, and all three registry records say so in their own words: CREDENCE counts DOUBLING OF SERUM CREATININE, DAPA-CKD counts a SUSTAINED DECLINE OF AT LEAST 50% IN eGFR, and EMPA-KIDNEY counts a SUSTAINED DECLINE OF AT LEAST 40% IN eGFR. Those are three different events. A 40% threshold admits strictly more patients than a 50% threshold, which admits strictly more than a doubling of creatinine, and the decline component is the largest contributor to each composite. The ESKD component differs too: CREDENCE and DAPA-CKD floor it at eGFR below 15, EMPA-KIDNEY at eGFR below 10. (2) THE STORED EFFECT MEASURE IS NOT THE MEASURE THE TRIALS REPORT. Every per-trial value in this object is an ODDS RATIO this project DERIVED from 2x2 counts, while all three trials analyse time to first occurrence -- DAPA-CKD's registry record states outright that 'the proportional hazards Cox regression model takes into account the time to the event', and the other two describe time-to-first-occurrence analyses. The index card published the derived odds ratio under the label HR. Neither ground can be repaired by re-pooling; both need the trials' own reported hazard ratios and a common endpoint.

pooled.withdrawn_reason: THE THREE TRIALS DO NOT SHARE ONE ENDPOINT DEFINITION, and each registry record says so in its own words. All three composites count kidney-function decline, but at three different thresholds: CREDENCE counts a DOUBLING OF SERUM CREATININE, DAPA-CKD counts a SUSTAINED DECLINE OF AT LEAST 50 PER CENT IN eGFR, and EMPA-KIDNEY counts a SUSTAINED DECLINE OF AT LEAST 40 PER CENT IN eGFR. Those are three different events, and the decline component is the largest contributor to each composite: a 40 per cent threshold admits strictly more patients than a 50 per cent threshold, which admits strictly more than a doubling of creatinine. The end-stage component differs too -- CREDENCE and DAPA-CKD floor it at an eGFR below 15, EMPA-KIDNEY at an eGFR below 10. SEPARATELY AND SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN: every per-trial value this review held was an ODDS RATIO DERIVED BY US from 2x2 counts, while all three trials analyse TIME TO FIRST OCCURRENCE -- DAPA-CKD's registry record states that 'the proportional hazards Cox regression model takes into account the time to the event'. The index card published that derived odds ratio under the label HR.
pooled.withdrawn_note: WHAT IS CONFIRMED, STATED AS PROMINENTLY AS WHAT IS WRONG. The component TYPES agree across all three trials: every one counts kidney-function decline, end-stage kidney disease, renal death and cardiovascular death, and every one counts the first of them to occur. EMPA-KIDNEY's registry TITLE names only 'kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death' and its DESCRIPTION places renal death and the eGFR thresholds inside 'kidney disease progression' -- so reading the title alone would have made it look like a trial counting no renal death at all, which would have argued for splitting it from the other two for the wrong reason. The full description is quoted on every trial for exactly that reason. These three trials are close; they are not the same, and the difference is a threshold rather than a missing component. AND THE THREE RESULTS AGREE: crude risk ratios of 0.72, 0.63 and 0.77, all in the same direction. AGREEMENT OF RESULTS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A COMMON ESTIMAND. What is averaged is decided by what was counted, not by how the counts came out, and this withdrawal cannot be undone by observing that the numbers are close. THE REPLACEMENT QUESTION IS IDENTIFIED AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: end-stage kidney disease as dialysis or transplant, and cardiovascular death, are each defined identically across all three and each is reported separately by all three. Taking it needs the trials' own reported hazard ratios for those components, from the registry RESULTS sections, and -- as recorded on ABLATION_AF -- a replacement question must be chosen before its answer is known. It is parked as a decision, not left as an oversight.

primary.what_is_confirmed_not_only_what_is_wrong: STATED AS PROMINENTLY AS THE PROBLEM, because a page that lists only what it found wrong misrepresents what it checked. THE COMPONENT TYPES AGREE ACROSS ALL THREE TRIALS. Every one counts kidney-function decline, end-stage kidney disease, renal death and cardiovascular death, and every one counts the first of them to occur. EMPA-KIDNEY's title names only 'kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death' and its DESCRIPTION places renal death inside kidney disease progression -- so reading the title alone would have made it look like a trial that counts no renal death, and would have argued for splitting it from the other two. That is the bare-TITLE-with-components-in-the-DESCRIPTION trap already in the ledger, and it is why the description is quoted here in full for every trial. These trials are close. They are not identical, and the difference is a threshold rather than a missing component.
primary.withheld_display: No pooled estimate is displayed. The value previously published on the index card, HR 0.68 (0.60-0.77) k=3, was a DERIVED ODDS RATIO labelled as a hazard ratio, over three composites with three different kidney-decline thresholds.
primary.replacement_question_identified_not_take: IDENTIFIED AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN. The obvious poolable question is the component route: end-stage kidney disease as dialysis or transplant, and cardiovascular death, are each defined identically across all three trials and each is reported separately by all three. That is the move the published literature made on the ablation topic and the move our own page failed to make there. It is not taken here for the reason recorded on ABLATION_AF: A REPLACEMENT QUESTION MUST BE CHOSEN BEFORE ITS ANSWER IS KNOWN, and it needs the trials' own reported hazard ratios for those components, which are in the registry RESULTS sections and were not retrieved in this pass. Parked as a decision, not left as an oversight.
primary.what_this_withdrawal_does_not_establish: NOT that the three trials disagree. Their crude risk ratios are 0.72, 0.63 and 0.77 and point the same way. AGREEMENT OF RESULTS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A COMMON ESTIMAND, and it is the reason this page cannot be rescued by observing that the numbers are close: what is being averaged is decided by what was counted, not by how the counts came out. NOT that pooling these trials is wrong in principle -- syntheses that pool each trial's own primary composite exist and are defensible when they SAY that is what they are doing. What is not defensible is presenting the result as one endpoint under one measure label.
